newsitem.title: USA: Spalding Cty, Ga., seeks 2nd tax bill for bonds.
newsitem.headline: Spalding Cty, Ga., seeks 2nd tax bill for bonds.

text.p: Georgia's Griffin-Spalding County School Board has asked the county to issue a second set of property tax bills because millage for a newly approved school bond issue was ommited from the first, the Griffin Daily News said Friday.
The $41 million general obligation bond issue for schools was approved on Tuesday.

School board members said they thought the property tax commissioner had been asked to delay sending the bills until after the referendum, so the extra 2.01 mills for debt service could be added if the measure passed.
But the bills were mailed out four days before the referendum, without the added millage, the newspaper said.
The County Commission is scheduled to decide on Oct 1 whether to honor the school board's request to send a secound round of property tax bills with the added millage.

The bond documents specify that the first $1.6 million debt service payment is due in August. If the county does not agree to send supplemental bills, the school board would be forced to cut construction projects or operating costs by $1.6 million to make up the difference in its budget, the newspaper said.
If the request for a supplementary bill is granted, the school board could be asked to pay the added costs for postage and collections.

"I think they dropped the ball in not letting our tax commissioner know they were going to need that tax if this passed," County Commission Chairman Bob Smith told the newspaper. "I tend to think they ought to pay their own way rather than asking us to."
The bonds are to be underwritten by Knox, Wall & Co of Atlanta. An employee there said the issue date had not been set.
